claims.statement: For every ordinary tree T and original leaf v with support s, Delta_j(T)=Delta_j(T-v)+Delta_(j-1)(T-{v,s}) for every integer j under zero extension; hence Delta_x(T)<0 forces at least one of Delta_x(T-v), Delta_(x-1)(T-{v,s}) to be negative for each v. This is a rank-local alternative, not a transfer to p>=x+2.
claims.scope: Exact deletion identity and its sign alternative at the first strict descent for finite ordinary trees; the K_(1,3) example only refutes the unguarded later-rank implication and is outside the primary eligibility region.
claims.reason: The polynomial partition by whether the original leaf is chosen proves the identity coefficientwise. The exact example shows the unrestricted proposed later-rank closure fails, but its rank is ineligible; no conclusion is drawn for the assigned aggregate.

limitations: No cross-rank transfer theorem was proved for eligible p satisfying x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1.
The counterexample K_(1,3) violates the strict lower-region alpha guard and is not a primary counterexample.
No eligible proper-selector witness, full favorable set with positive aggregate, or proof of the primary global inequality is supplied.
No assumption of forest unimodality, log-concavity, or no-recovery is used.
